Providing support for X different version is time consuming, annoying, and - most importantly - expensive as all fucks. If every single one of your clients uses the same version (or marginally different) of software, you can pinpoint and solve problems easier, faster and cheaper.
What do you think is the other reason FAQs often contain the advice to update your software? To keep you at the same level of technology people trying to fix your shit are.

Since everyone here is making assumptions, I'll take a swing at answering this for you, OP: nobody knows except for Microsoft engineers and executives.

Microsoft plays a lot of their strategies really close to the chest, so they haven't really explained anything with Win10, which is one reason so many people hate it. It's DEFINITELY the reason I first raised an eyebrow when Win10 was in its testing period...

First, Microsoft said that the Win10 "upgrade" would be free for the "lifetime of the machine" for the "user," but M$ UTTERLY REFUSED to define these terms/phrases. This is dangerous because they could change their definitions, and now you need to pay for a machine you've owned for three years, or else it won't work. Let's say you have a gaming machine you built yourself, upgraded from Win7 to Win10, and decided to change out some of your hardware for newer/better stuff... you change your HDD for an SDD, the RAM, the video card, and the power brick... is this the same machine, or does your "old machine" consist of more than the motherboard? What is M$'s formula for which parts consist of the machine, and how fast/rapidly you change them in the "lifetime of the machine?"

Then, they inserted telemetry which took a screenshot and tracked your keystrokes... their rationale was nebulous and didn't explain why it was necessary for this level of invasiveness when testing the new release. They said that this was to help them track any potential problems with their new OS, but there are plenty of upgrades that successfully do this without literally screencapping and keylogging everything their users are doing. Many user cried foul, and M$ hasn't really made many changes to their telemetry system... they said they've removed this logging software, but who really knows, other than the engineers and executives? Again, back to the beginning of my post...

Next, they announced that updates would no longer be avoidable, and would be COMPLETELY out of the user's control... unless you had an Enterprise version, in which case you could only selectively delay updates by 6 months. In other words, M$ could install what they wanted, when they wanted, and remove anything at any time without your consent. I can't control it, and that means that it's not really MY machine anymore... and a lot of other people feel the same.

The list goes on and on, but M$ has run this same play over and over again, and a lot of users (especially around VOAT) have shied away from these "clandestine" tactics. M$ has stated that Win10 is going to be the final, rolling-release (like OSX is to Apple), and that it's the most secure... which is their excuse for why they're pushing the OS so hard. But, like above, that's a nebulous answer to a big problem, and many users are weary of the M$ bullshit.

Some say it's about money, some say it's about control, and some have other (smaller) theories. But unless they're M$ software engineers or executives, they'll never know for sure. Unless they're in one of those two groups, they're just making guesses... some would call them "educated guesses," but that doesn't change the fact that it's still a guess. I know that sounds terrible, but that's all we have... guesses. Because M$ is being so secretive about everything they're doing, all we can do is guess as to why.
